text: The president, this whole time, he was talking about what's happening in Ukraine, right? He was giving his speech, saying that they're mobilizing soldiers in Ukraine, recruiting people practically off the streets, like dogs. He used some pretty harsh language. Then he talked about how they're throwing them into the fire, using them as expendable material and so on. And a significant part of his speech was devoted to all these issues surrounding Ukraine. As a citizen of the Russian Federation, I'll be honest with you. I wasn't interested in listening to a history lesson about whose land it is or isn't, especially since it really is a matter of debate, and, well, now is not the time to talk about it. As for Zelensky being prepared to make concessions on territory, de facto it's Ukrainian territory, whether people like it or not. And Zelensky, despite how much I dislike the man who put me under Ukrainian sanctions, I have no love for Zelensky, but he's completely… I mean, I understand what he means. He's prepared to give up part of Ukraine's territory in exchange for some kind of agreement to end the war. I understand his logic. Why start telling us that it's already our territory anyway? Why talk about how we're two brotherly peoples? How genetic studies have confirmed that we're two brotherly peoples? Well, yes, we're two brotherly peoples. But really, we all descended from Adam and Eve, from the first people on earth, and broadly speaking, we're all related. Distantly, very distantly, but we're related. By that logic, you could say that too. I mean, in church they say brothers and sisters. Before God, there is neither Greek nor Roman. Let's remember the Holy Scriptures. And if Putin is a believer, surely he remembers that phrase. So, to say in this speech right now that we're brothers? Well, yes, but what does that have to do with the matter at hand? Why say it? I want to hear our position in these negotiations. Not a history lesson or a discussion of how soldiers are being recruited into the Ukrainian army. And if we're going to talk about that, well, let's also remember Pusilin's mobilization here. How they recruited students, young guys from Donetsk, 20 to 25 years old, 19 to 25. Why doesn't Putin talk about that? How they were called up under the pretext of military training just before the start of the special military operation, and then suddenly bang, the war began. And where did they all end up? Come on, let's talk about that. Let's talk about recruiting people from prisons. A few years ago, before the special military operation, remember how our propagandists were constantly pointing their fingers at the Ukrainian armed forces and saying, look, Look, look how bad things are for them. They're already recruiting people from prisons. They've got no army left. They're taking criminals into the army. And what about us now? Excuse me, but I'd like to ask an impertinent question. My son went into the army from prison and ended up there, so to speak. I'm not going to reveal all the details on air right now, but he came from prison. And there are tens of thousands like him there. Not hundreds. Tens of thousands. tens of thousands. And as for how they're treated at the front, you know, you don't need to tell me about that, respected Mr. President, or perhaps not so respected Mr. President. I know how people who went from prison to the Special Military Operation are treated. And I also know how long they survive on average at the front, including from what officers have told me. The average life expectancy of a prisoner in the zone of the Special Military Operation. Doesn't that happen here? Where did the expression meet assaults come from? Where did it come from? Did it come to us from Ukraine? Meet assaults? No. That's our Russian invention, so to speak. Forgive the dark, the dark irony. It was here that our soldiers were sent into frontal assaults by particularly outstanding generals like Lopin, who was later awarded the title Hero of Russia and was the face of United Russia in the recent elections, if you can even call that whole thing by that name. Remember how he tried to cross that river several times? Even Kadyrov called him out for it. Officers were criticizing him behind the scenes too, talking about his abilities as a commander. Was he held accountable for that? For the deaths? For the deaths of a huge number of people and the loss of equipment that was burned? I mean, what kind of thinking does it take to cross a river at the same spot when the enemy has already zeroed in on it? They crossed once, they were beaten back. The enemy had the spot zeroed in and they went to cross the river again, then went a third time. Was he held accountable? No. So why tell me now that Ukrainians are being sent to the front as expendable material? Is it any different here? Have a look. Respected, or not so respected, Mr. President, at the internet you're slowing down, at that very same YouTube. Just look up videos from the other side, posted by Ukrainian army units. See what the war actually looks like. And then don't tell us that things are somehow different on our side. Remember Yegor Lipov? I'm sure it's the same for them, and everything is going according to plan. That's what's really happening, as I see it. Everything is going according to plan. The only question is, whose plan is it all going according to? Is this how it's supposed to be? More than a million. More than a million. Yesterday I was with some Serbian friends. We sat and talked. Remarkable people with a remarkable love for us Russians and enormous pain in their hearts over what's happening. They really, I saw it in their eyes. Tears were welling up in their eyes as we talked when I told them that by our journalistic estimates, based on indirect evidence, these are not proven figures of course, they're rough estimates, more than a million people have been killed, wounded or gone missing on both sides. And the overwhelming majority of those killed, wounded, or missing are Russians. Russians are dying on both sides. Putin can say whatever he wants about history, referendums, or anything else, but the fact is that Russians are dying today. The total number of people who have died as a result of the Special Military Operation is already greater than the losses during the Civil War. I mean at the front during the Civil War, not those who died of typhus or starvation. Fewer people died at the front in the Civil War. Killed, wounded, missing. Fewer. By our rough estimates, based on indirect evidence, fewer than in the course of the special military operation on both sides. I want to emphasize that again. On both sides. If Russians are dying, then what's the point of all this talk? We simply need to stop the war. It's the fifth year now. How much longer are you going to keep pursuing the goals set for the special military operation? How many human lives are you prepared to give up? Is anyone from your inner circle at the front? My son is at the front. I have the right to say this. The one thing I told him when he ended up there was, do everything you can to keep blood off your hands. Please, try. I understand it's a war, but I'm asking you. please let your hands remain clean if that's possible.
